messages:
sara_support: Heads-up — a customer (FinEdge) just flagged that after yesterday's model bump some assistant responses are noticeably shorter and omit follow-up questions. They're not calling it 'broken', but it's causing misunderstandings in multi-step flows.

omar_eng: Can you paste a pair of before/after examples and the exact time of their first bad observation? Also which model & rollout?

sara_support: Sent by customer at 22:12 UTC. They said rollout id r-2026-03-16-19. They included two examples. Prompt + expected (old) vs actual (new).

sara_support: ```
prompt: "Help me draft a short onboarding email for a new user who signed up but didn't verify their account. Tone: friendly, helpful. Include next steps and a one-line CTA."
old_response (v1.0.24): "Hi there! Welcome — we're excited to have you. Before you can get started, please verify your email by clicking the link we sent. If you didn't receive it, check spam or request a new one from your account settings. Once verified, you'll be able to access your dashboard and start the quick setup wizard. Need me to draft a subject line too?"
new_response (v1.0.25): "Welcome! Please verify your email to continue. If you didn't get it, request a new one."
```

sara_support: The customer said the new response is fine for short prompts but loses the optional clarifier and CTA which they rely on in templating pipelines.

omar_eng: Interesting — that's not a hard failure, it's a behavioral regression (verbosity/drop of optional offers). Could be a response-length bias or decoding-temp change. Did the rollout change decoding defaults?

maya_prod: r-2026-03-16-19 was a partial canary for v1.0.25. It included a small decoding tweak: default top_p clamped at 0.9 for safety and a prompt compression step for instruction normalization. Both were rolled into canary at 19:00 UTC and promoted at 21:45 UTC.

ryan_oncall: tagging deploy-bot for timeline. @deploy-bot please confirm canary->prod times.

deploy-bot: canary r-2026-03-16-19 promoted to prod at 2026-03-16T21:45:12Z (verified).

omar_eng: That prompt compression could remove trailing offers like "Need me to draft a subject line too?" if heuristics consider it optional. Also clamping top_p can make outputs more conservative. We should repro locally with both model variants and exact decoding settings.

sara_support: Customer attached 12 more examples where 'offer to help' and short clarifying q's were trimmed. They say this affects ~4% of generated templates, causing missing CTAs in transactional messages.

omar_eng: Repro steps for us: 1) checkout model v1.0.24 and v1.0.25. 2) run prompt above with identical request parameters (temperature 0.2, top_p 1.0). 3) compare outputs. If the platform is overriding top_p to 0.9 in v1.0.25, that'll explain.

maya_prod: We did an internal check: platform config was supposed to respect per-request decoding params, but a conservative safety patch accidentally clamped top_p for requests originating from the hosted API default route. That was enabled in VCL rule set at 18:59 UTC and not intended for requests with explicit top_p.

ryan_oncall: Oof. That matches. Action plan?

omar_eng: Short-term: roll back the VCL clamp and re-run a canary for 30 mins. Medium-term: add a unit test to ensure explicit decoding params are honored and add a regression test asserting optional clarifier retention on a prompt corpus.

sara_support: Customer asked for mitigation while we investigate. They requested a temporary flag or a model parameter override so their templates use v1.0.24 until resolved.

maya_prod: We can pin their org to v1.0.24 for 24–72 hours and open an SR to schedule a managed rollback. I'll prepare the support opt-in link.

sara_support: I'll offer the pin and ask for example IDs where missing CTAs led to user-facing issues. Also asked whether they'd like a live call.

omar_eng: For follow-up: gather a small eval set of ~50 proxy prompts, run A/B between v1.0.24 and v1.0.25 with identical decoding params and flag cases where v1.0.25 output is substrings of v1.0.24 (indicative of pruning). Share the diff stats here.

ryan_oncall: Logging note: created ticket INF-4621 (verbosity-regression) and linked rollout r-2026-03-16-19.

sara_support: Customer update queued: offering pin + ETA for investigation. Keeping thread open for repro artifacts and final resolution. :white_check_mark:
